findings.where: Phone first screen: Mark's line, the yellow address strip and the supporting paragraph ("I advise multilateral development banks…")
findings.fault: On the phone the yellow address strip sits between the large line and the paragraph that explains it. On desktop the order is line, paragraph, then address. Here the paragraph saying who Mark advises and on what is cut off from its heading by the strip and lands after the ask, at the foot of the frame, where it reads like an afterthought. Proximity breaks: the heading and its explanation no longer read as one statement.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer opening the site on a phone from a shared link. They are asked to write to Mark before the page has told them what he does, and the sentence that would have earned the email comes only after it.

findings.where: Phone, Motion specimen: the four-column timing table (Element · Start · Length · Easing)
findings.fault: At 390 px all four columns stay side by side, so the Element column shrinks to a strip one or two words wide. "Mark's line settles: opacity 0 to 1 as it rises 0.16 em…" breaks into seven ragged lines, and the Easing value breaks mid-token ("cubic- / bezier(0.3,"). The table ends up much taller than its content and hard to scan.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile on a phone. The motion spec is one of the parts they judge, and they have to piece each row back together.

findings.where: Desktop, Motion specimen: the easing-curve box and its caption below
findings.fault: The curve box's left edge sits a few pixels right of the shared left edge (x≈426) that every other specimen part keeps, including the caption directly beneath it. The column edge visibly steps at the one place where a box and a line of text are stacked.
findings.who_objects: A designer or the founder scanning the specimen column. The sheet's selling point is a document's exactness, and an edge that is off by a nudge undercuts it.
